question: Should OpenClaw adopt this broad shared localization runtime and release-readiness policy in core as a staged five-PR program, or should the work be narrowed to independently reviewable surface fixes first?
rationale: The branch introduces a new shared package, Gateway metadata contract, coverage policy, and release-readiness gates across many owners; code review alone cannot determine the desired permanent product and ownership boundary.

options.title: Stage the core localization program
options.body: Accept the shared direction in principle, then require each foundation PR to be independently rebased, reviewed, compatibility-validated, and proven before the next lands.

options.title: Narrow to targeted localization fixes
options.body: Keep the immediate user-visible fixes but defer the shared registry, maturity matrix, and fail-closed readiness policy until an RFC-backed core decision is complete.

recommendation.title: Stage the core localization program
recommendation.body: Accept the shared direction in principle, then require each foundation PR to be independently rebased, reviewed, compatibility-validated, and proven before the next lands.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor owns the proposed five-PR series and is the only concrete routing candidate present in the supplied feature history; repository owners should make the final product decision.
